title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer thresholds during regional failover to prevent thrashing
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: During yesterday's regional failover exercise we observed the SLO enforcer oscillating between open/closed states when downstream capacity in the target region was still warming up. The root cause was overly-aggressive thresholds and insufficient hysteresis in the regional failover path which caused frequent load-shedding toggles and increased error budget burn for a subset of customers. This hotfix introduces conservative adjustments to the enforcer's regional thresholds and adds a short-circuit backoff (grace period) after a failover transition to prevent immediate re-enablement. Changes are scoped to the enforcer control path and observability rules; behavior is behind a feature flag (slo_enforcer:regional_hysteresis) that is enabled by default for main and will be backported to release-2026-02. Summary of changes: updated threshold math to use a 60s smoothing window, increase per-region error-rate threshold by 20% during cold-warm transitions, add a 30s post-failover hold period before lifting load-shedding for any affected route, add quorum check for cross-region metrics to avoid single-metric oscillation, and expose new metrics (slo_enforcer.hold_count, slo_enforcer.smoothing_window_ms). Also tightened related alerting and added integration tests reproducing the warm-up scenario. Testing: unit tests cover the threshold math and backoff logic; integration test simulates a regional capacity ramp using the perf-canary harness. Ran end-to-end in staging against a canary customer and observed stable failover with no thrashing. CI initially had one flaky test (TestTracePropagation) which failed in the first run; re-ran CI and all checks passed. Rollout and mitigation: squash-merged to main and will be cherry-picked to release-2026-02 and release-2026-01 as hotfixes. We can toggle the feature flag per-cluster if any regressions are observed. Related tickets/links: Linear ENG-3421 (SLO enforcer thrashing), ENG-3499 (regional failover follow-up), SUP-4982 (customer incident linked).
